summary: [standards] The lock-file sharing is right: under nextest (9 tests, 6 slow) the first test ran the checker once, wrote atip_check-canon-l1.json under target/tmp/atip-report/<NEXTEST_RUN_ID>/ and the three waiters finished together at 260 s with the result of that one run (shim count 4 = 1 + 3 planted); under cargo test the LazyLock does the same (4). No .partial file is left and the publish is a rename under the lock. Two small things: the run directories under target/tmp/atip-report are never removed, and if the first test panics inside the run each waiter takes the lock in turn and reruns the checker. Also the atip-profile junit (timestamp 19:57, run 39 min) is older than the commit (20:42) although the evidence says `from the clean worktree at the commit`; atip-check is unchanged since, and my own run of the crate at HEAD stands in for it. `cargo nextest run -p atip-check` under the default profile runs nothing (the default-filter): use --profile atip.
